examples.en: Yesterday evening I watched a movie with a friend.
My head has been hurting since last evening.
Did you watch the nine o'clock news last evening?
Last evening it rained a lot.
I'm really sorry about what happened last evening.
Up until last evening the weather was fine.

explain: '어젯밤'은 잠자기 전 늦은 시간의 느낌이 강하고, '어제저녁'은 저녁 식사 무렵처럼 조금 이른 시간을 말할 때 잘 어울려요. 뒤에 '에'를 붙이거나 생략해도 돼요. '어제 저녁'처럼 띄어 쓴 형태로도 많이 봐요.

phrases.en: I went to bed late last night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어제저녁'보다 더 늦은 시간, 잠자기 전을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a later time than '어제저녁', closer to bedtime.

phrases.en: My stomach has hurt since last evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어제저녁에 시작해서 지금까지 이어지는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something that started last evening and continues now.

phrases.en: I met my friend at six o'clock yesterday evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구체적인 시간과 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used together with a specific time.

explain_en: '어젯밤' feels like late hours close to bedtime, while '어제저녁' suits an earlier time, around dinner. You can add '에' after it or leave it out. You will also often see it written with a space, as '어제 저녁'.
